architecture: small CNN: conv5x5(7->16, pad 2) relu maxpool2, conv5x5(16->32, pad 2) relu maxpool2, conv3x3(32->64, pad 1) relu, global average pool, fc 64->64 relu, fc 64->10

input.layout: channel (band), row (north at the top), column (west at the left); 20 m pixels, 640 x 640 m
input.scaling: x = value / 10000, where value is the mean of a 2 x 2 block of Sentinel-2 Level-1C digital numbers (top-of-atmosphere reflectance x 10000) rounded to an integer; so x is top-of-atmosphere reflectance, mostly between 0 and 0.5 (bright clouds, snow and roofs can exceed it)

dataset_facts: EuroSAT (Helber et al. 2019): 27,000 labelled 64 x 64 patches at 10 m from Sentinel-2 Level-1C images over 34 European countries, 2,000 to 3,000 per class, all 13 bands resampled to 10 m. Here 7 bands are kept and each 2 x 2 block is averaged, giving 32 x 32 pixels at 20 m. Each patch shows one land use or cover class; the dataset's authors selected the patches with reference land-use data and checked them by hand; scenes are mostly cloud-free and cover all seasons.
conv: cross-correlation as in PyTorch Conv2d: out[o, i, j] = bias[o] + sum_c sum_u sum_v weight[o, c, u, v] * in[c, i + u, j + v] (after zero padding)
global_average_pool: g[c] = the mean of the 64 values of channel c of the [64, 8, 8] map
output: 10 logits, class k = the k-th entry of classes; the prediction is the argmax (logits within 1e-9 x max(1, |max logit|) of the maximum count as tied; ties go to the lowest index)
metric: accuracy on 4,000 held-out patches, 400 per class
